title: Cost ledger line (gtm/api-calls.jsonl)
description: The honest cost record. An estimate echoed back as an actual is worse than an admitted estimate — it is the old honor-system math moved into JavaScript.

credits_estimated_if_billed.description: Present ONLY on a line that was not billed. The price the call would have carried had it been billed. Deliberately not `credits_estimated`: every consumer sums that field, so a would-have-been price living there overstated spend and could stop a run on a ceiling it never reached.

billed.description: Did this call cost credits? false for a non-2xx (billing rule) and for a 2xx whose body says `billed: false` (the provider errored). null means UNKNOWN — http_status 0 is a response never seen, and a request the server may have processed must not be booked at zero.

not_billed_reason.description: Why nothing was charged. `provider_error` is NOT a not-found: the row was never looked up and must be retried.

cost_status.description: `actual` = a real charge was read from the response. `estimated_unverifiable` = the response omits the billing field (11 of 21 metered endpoints); NEVER write `actual` from an estimate. `known_zero` = the rule says no charge occurred (a non-2xx deducts no credits), which is distinct from having verified one.

balance_after.description: populated free from any 402 body (reserved + balance) or a cached GET /usage

estimate_basis.description: How credits_estimated was derived, e.g. '10 base + 0.5/result x 25' or 'assumed 25 results/page'. For the 11 endpoints whose charge is never verifiable the estimate is the ONLY number, so a reader must be able to tell a firm flat price from a page-size guess. The session receipt reuses this math.

row_id.description: Joins a ledger line back to its journal unit. Without row_id + hop, reconcile() can only compare per-run totals and a per-row cost audit is impossible across the two files.

$comment: Session end reconciles the sum against GET /usage and reports drift, once the API documents a usage endpoint. The /richapi-gtm receipt reuses this math — no fork — and an eval fails CI on any receipt claim exceeding ledger actuals.
